paths: postgresql schema pipeline_lab_<12 hex characters> in the DATABASE_URL database, created and dropped by each test run
cleanup.notes: Setup creates the virtual environment .venv in the lab folder (the README creates and activates it before the setup command) and installs the exact versions pinned in starter/requirements.txt, the lab's lock of every installed package; psycopg comes with its binary package so no compiler or libpq install is needed. The database checks read DATABASE_URL, create one uniquely named schema pipeline_lab_<12 hex characters> in that database, run starter/pipeline/schema.sql inside it, and drop it with CASCADE when the module's tests finish; they never touch another schema. After an interrupted run the README lists and drops leftover pipeline_lab_ schemas. The test command writes .pytest_cache and __pycache__ folders; the Task 10 check starts child Python processes with bytecode writing off and the pytest cache plugin disabled. The enrichment uses the shipped FakeModelClient with scripted answers: no network, API key, account or paid AI call. The random schema suffix only isolates runs and never changes a result; every check uses fixed data and fixed timestamps. Resetting the learner's work means copying the four edited files back from a fresh copy of the lab. The expected output replaces the per-learner test count and the run time with placeholders, because Task 10 adds the learner's own tests to the run. The 55-minute median is a task-by-task authoring estimate of the ten tasks, not a measured learner pilot; 60 minutes is the cap of the 30-60 minute module-lab allowance, inside the two Lab days' guided-lab blocks. The checks observe yielded records, rows in PostgreSQL, validation results, prompts sent to the fake client and log records; they also check the source for the taught construct (yield, csv.DictReader, json.loads, an explicit encoding, ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE, executemany, a WITH common table expression, DISTINCT ON or ROW_NUMBER), and Task 10 runs the learner's tests against their code and against two broken versions of enrich.
